vulnerability_types.name: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) Policy Not Enabled
vulnerability_types.impact: HSTS can be used to prevent and/or mitigate some types of man-in-the-middle (MitM) attacks
vulnerability_types.description:
HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) tells a browser that a web site is only accessable using HTTPS.
        
        It was detected that your web application doesn't implement HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) as the Strict Transport Security header is missing from the response.
vulnerability_types.recommendation: It's recommended to implement HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) into your web application. Consult web references for more information

vulnerability_types.impact: This SSL certificate is not valid.
vulnerability_types.description:
One of the TLS/SSL certificates sent by your server has either expired or is not yet valid.

Most web browsers will present end-users with a security warning, asking them to manually confirm the authenticity of your certificate chain. Software or automated systems may silently refuse to connect to the server.

This alert is not necessarily caused by the server (leaf) certificate, but may have been triggered by an intermediate certificate. Please refer to the certificate serial number in the alert details to identify the affected certificate.
vulnerability_types.recommendation: Verify Start Date and/or End Dates of your SSL Certificate.

vulnerability_types.name: Cookies Not Marked as HttpOnly
vulnerability_types.impact: Cookies can be accessed by client-side scripts.
vulnerability_types.description: One or more cookies don't have the HttpOnly flag set. When a cookie is set with the HttpOnly flag, it instructs the browser that the cookie can only be accessed by the server and not by client-side scripts. This is an important security protection for session cookies.
vulnerability_types.recommendation: If possible, you should set the HttpOnly flag for these cookies.

vulnerability_types.name: Version Disclosure (PHP)
vulnerability_types.impact: An attacker might use the disclosed information to harvest specific security vulnerabilities for the version identified.
vulnerability_types.description: The web server is sending the X-Powered-By: response headers, revealing the PHP version.
vulnerability_types.recommendation: Configure your web server to prevent information leakage from its HTTP response.

vulnerability_types.name: Content Security Policy (CSP) Not Implemented
vulnerability_types.impact: CSP can be used to prevent and/or mitigate attacks that involve content/code injection, such as cross-site scripting/XSS attacks, attacks that require embedding a malicious resource, attacks that involve malicious use of iframes, such as clickjacking attacks, and others.
vulnerability_types.description:
Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks.

Content Security Policy (CSP) can be implemented by adding a Content-Security-Policy header. The value of this header is a string containing the policy directives describing your Content Security Policy. To implement CSP, you should define lists of allowed origins for the all of the types of resources that your site utilizes. For example, if you have a simple site that needs to load scripts, stylesheets, and images hosted locally, as well as from the jQuery library from their CDN, the CSP header could look like the following: 

Content-Security-Policy:
    default-src 'self';
    script-src 'self' https://code.jquery.com;


It was detected that your web application doesn't implement Content Security Policy (CSP) as the CSP header is missing from the response. It's recommended to implement Content Security Policy (CSP) into your web application.
vulnerability_types.recommendation: It's recommended to implement Content Security Policy (CSP) into your web application. Configuring Content Security Policy involves adding the Content-Security-Policy HTTP header to a web page and giving it values to control resources the user agent is allowed to load for that page.

vulnerability_types.name: Generic Email Address Disclosure
vulnerability_types.impact: Email addresses posted on Web sites may attract spam.
vulnerability_types.description: One or more email addresses have been found on this website. The majority of spam comes from email addresses harvested off the internet. The spam-bots (also known as email harvesters and email extractors) are programs that scour the internet looking for email addresses on any website they come across.  Spambot programs look for strings like myname@mydomain.com and then record any addresses found.
vulnerability_types.recommendation: Check references for details on how to solve this problem.

vulnerability_types.name: Outdated JavaScript libraries
vulnerability_types.description: You are using an outdated version of one or more JavaScript libraries. A more recent version is available. Although your version was not found to be affected by any security vulnerabilities, it is recommended to keep libraries up to date.

vulnerability_types.name: Permissions-Policy header not implemented
vulnerability_types.description: The Permissions-Policy header allows developers to selectively enable and disable use of various browser features and APIs.
